## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Run once if needed:
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "maps"))

library(tidyverse)
library(maps)

# 1. Read Grambank data directly from GitHub
base_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/",
  "main/data/2026/2026-11-03/"
)

languages <- read_csv(
  paste0(base_url, "grambank_languages.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

parameters <- read_csv(
  paste0(base_url, "grambank_parameters.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

values <- read_csv(
  paste0(base_url, "grambank_values.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# 2. Check the feature definition
parameters |>
  filter(parameter_id == "GB051") |>
  select(parameter_id, feature_name) |>
  print()

# 3. Keep language varieties with a recorded GB051 value
gender <- values |>
  filter(parameter_id == "GB051", value %in% c(0L, 1L)) |>
  inner_join(languages, by = "language_id")

# 4. Export the language varieties with masculine and feminine noun genders
languages_with_gender <- gender |>
  filter(value == 1L) |>
  select(language_name, macroarea, family_name, glottocode) |>
  arrange(macroarea, language_name)

print(languages_with_gender)
write_csv(languages_with_gender, "languages_with_masculine_feminine_gender.csv")

# 5. Calculate regional percentages
regional_summary <- gender |>
  filter(!is.na(macroarea)) |>
  group_by(macroarea) |>
  summarise(
    with_gender = sum(value == 1L),
    total_recorded = n(),
    percent = round(100 * with_gender / total_recorded, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(percent))

print(regional_summary)

# 6. Prepare the world map and language locations
world <- map_data("world")

map_points <- gender |>
  drop_na(longitude, latitude) |>
  arrange(value)  # Draw blue points last where points overlap

# 7. Draw the map
gender_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = world,
    aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "grey95",
    color = "grey82",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = map_points,
    aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = factor(value)),
    size = 1.1,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("1" = "#0072B2", "0" = "#D55E00"),
    breaks = c("1", "0"),
    labels = c(
  "With masculine and feminine noun genders",
  "Without masculine and feminine noun genders"
)
  ) +
  coord_fixed(
    xlim = c(-183, 183),
    ylim = c(-92, 92),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Where do languages distinguish masculine and feminine noun genders?",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "They are most common in Australia (33%) and least common in Papunesia (10%) "),
    caption = "By Bowen Tang , Data from Grambank via TidyTuesday (November 3, 2026)"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey35"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0, color = "grey45"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.margin = margin(12, 12, 12, 12)
  )

print(gender_map)

# 8. Save the full map
ggsave(
  filename = "grambank-noun-gender.png",
  plot = gender_map,
  width = 12,
  height = 7.2,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
parameters |>
  filter(parameter_id == "GB051") |>
  View()
```
